description: An interactive Kubernetes log viewer for your terminal.

summary.one_liner: kl is an interactive terminal viewer for Kubernetes logs that can show, search, and archive logs across multiple containers, pods, namespaces, and clusters.
summary.what_it_does: kl runs in a terminal and lets you pick Kubernetes containers interactively or auto-select them by regex matching on names, labels, and pod owners. It can interleave logs from several containers by timestamp and watch cluster changes in real time. Logs can be searched by exact string or regex, with optional surrounding context, and structured logs can be pretty-printed inline. A zoom view lets you step through individual pretty-printed log entries, and you can save a view to a file or copy a log to the clipboard. Color themes are included, with an accessible ANSI default, a classic theme, and a no-color option.
use_cases: tail logs from multiple pods at once
view logs across several Kubernetes clusters
filter container logs by name or label pattern
pretty-print JSON logs in a terminal
save or share pod logs to a file
notable: Auto-selects containers by regex against names, labels, and pod owners
Interleaves logs from multiple containers by timestamp
Multi-cluster and multi-namespace viewing in one session
Inline pretty-printing of structured logs and per-entry zoom
Accessible ANSI color themes with a no-color option
caveats: Development setup for testing requires k3d and a sample deployment, and the README does not describe other requirements
Install options vary by platform and some are third-party packages (nix, AUR, winget, scoop, chocolatey)
